title: IMF warns Brazil’s stablecoin activity outpaces traditional capital flows
summary: The IMF said Brazil’s stablecoin market has expanded rapidly since 2017, with cross-border crypto flows growing faster than traditional capital flows.

title: Lido upgrade aims to slash Ethereum’s validator count by one-third
summary: Lido launched Curated Module v2, an upgrade that could reduce Ethereum’s validator count by one-third by consolidating validators and introducing new operator rules.

title: Ondo shifts from layer-1 blockchain plan to offchain execution network
summary: The new system marks an apparent departure from the institution-focused layer-1 blockchain Ondo announced in 2025.

title: Apple faces lawsuit over alleged $1.8M Bitcoin wallet app losses
summary: Three users allege a fake Sparrow Wallet app on Apple’s App Store drained their Bitcoin holdings, with losses totaling more than $1.8 million.

title: Binance co-founder CZ backs crypto license passporting across ASEAN
summary: Binance co-founder CZ backed crypto license passporting across ASEAN to simplify approvals, reduce compliance costs and encourage competition.

title: US judge temporarily blocks Minnesota prediction market ban
summary: The preliminary injunction allows Kalshi and Polymarket US to continue operating in Minnesota while the court considers their challenge to the state law.

title: Zimbabwe admits 7 fintech projects to regulatory sandbox
summary: Sandbox participation permits supervised testing but does not guarantee full commercial registration.

title: Hong Kong prepares banks for quantum threats amid tokenization push
summary: The HKMA aims to make Hong Kong’s banking sector fully prepared for quantum-related security risks by 2030 as the city expands tokenized finance.

title: Binance phishes its own staff monthly, India censors BitChat code: Asia Express
summary: Binance has been phishing its own staff to get ahead of potential attacks. South Korean crypto volumes tank 89% — plus all of the week’s other crypto news from Asia.

title: New York AG warns CLARITY Act could weaken state crypto enforcement
summary: New York Attorney General Letitia James said the federal crypto market structure bill could restrict state regulators and urged Congress to impose stronger consumer protections on digital asset platforms.
